ieee_caption: End-to-end research architecture for urban taxi mobility pattern discovery, illustrating data ingestion, multi-stage cleaning, spatial discretization, Haversine DBSCAN clustering, PrefixSpan sequential mining, unified pair-level evaluation, and dashboard analytics.
Multi-stage trajectory preprocessing pipeline: raw log parsing, invalid coordinate purging, non-destructive out-of-region bounding, deduplication, chronological sorting, and speed anomaly validation.

Spatial analysis workflow: continuous GPS projection into 500 m equirectangular planar grid cells, pairwise Haversine distance matrix computation in radians, and DBSCAN hotspot cluster identification.

Sequential pattern mining workflow: grouping observations by taxi-day (taxi_id::date), compressing consecutive same-cell visits, building prefix-projected databases, mining frequent gapped subsequences, and extracting deduplicated ordered pairs.
UML use-case diagram depicting operational interactions among Fleet Analysts, Transit Planners, and Commuters within the dual-mode mobility analytics dashboard.

UML activity diagram illustrating end-to-end execution flow: data validation, trajectory segmentation, hotspot detection, sequential mining, chronological holdout splitting, and empirical reference evaluation.
UML sequence diagram showing message and data exchange between Streamlit UI, Analytical Orchestrators, Computational Engines (Spatial, PrefixSpan), and Data Storage.
K-distance graph (k = 15) for DBSCAN parameter calibration, illustrating the elbow inflection at epsilon = 300 m used to identify 237 urban activity hotspots.

Frequent pattern discovery count (logarithmic scale) and empirical reference precision, recall, and F1 across support thresholds (1.0%, 2.0%, 5.0%), demonstrating the trade-off between discovery volume and precision.
Effect of spatial discretization resolution (300 m, 500 m, 800 m) on active spatial vocabulary, point density, and frequent pattern volume at 5.0% minimum support.
Comparative precision, recall, and F1 across mining methods evaluated on the real T-Drive empirical reference benchmark, highlighting the impact of support tuning and composite score ranking.
Pair-level and pattern-level recovery performance of PrefixSpan across support thresholds on the objective synthetic benchmark, confirming 100% ground-truth planted corridor recovery.
Pipeline execution runtime and data throughput across nested fleet sample sizes (99, 249, 497 active taxis), demonstrating sub-minute execution up to 833,000 GPS points.
Diurnal urban taxi mobility profiles in Beijing, depicting normalized hourly GPS observation frequencies and time-segment distributions across weekdays and weekends.
